questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Academic opportunities

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: Especially, the cultural differences and experience of the US were crucial.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: It was super easy. UCPH were helpful before the arrival and a few weeks before arrival, I got in contact with people from UCSB, who were extremely helpful.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: I had some assistance with class registration and sports.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: It is not easy before arriving to Santa Barbara as you don't know what to look for and whether you are dealing with a scammer or not. There exist multiple groups on Facebook that can be helpful. However, these are mostly helpful when you have arrived in Santa Barbara.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: Isla Vista is the place to be. I lived at Del Playa Dr. This was a loud but fun street to experience. However, if you prefer to sleep more quietly, I suggest finding a place on either Sabado or Trigo. Also, be aware of the housing shortage so demand is high.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: It was not easy. First of all, American students are prioritized before exchange students. Secondly, the supply of economic courses are limited due to the need for prerequisites, which I spent a lot of time convincing the institution that my courses at UCPH had covered the demanded prereqs. If classes are full, it is common to crash classes. This means that you register as waitlisted and follow the class in the hope of getting a free spot.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: The professors were understanding and tried to help.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: Difficult to say. I wanted some other classes, but they were filled up before I even read about them.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Get in contact with EAP department and professors as soon as possible.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: Undergrad were pretty straight when attending the master at UCPH.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: Despite smaller class rooms it was close to being the same. Biggest difference was a more fast-paced structure with quarters and midterms.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Intramural Soccer was a great part of my exchange. Easiest way to be a part of this is through network. Befriend some american and ask them about intramural activities.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Soccer and partying in the backyards with the people in IV.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Travel the western coast. The nature is beautiful. Especially Yosemite National Park.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Kind of easy. Just be yourself and integrate that into the american culture.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Live with them. Get a spot with american students.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: The biggest difference was the fact that I was on exchange and every was just another ordinary day in their life. So local students don't have the same incentives to travel and experience. Or even go to the beach.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The laid back and casual California vibe.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
1) Find a housing spot with local students. But remember, first is not always best, so explore some different housing possibilities and get a place close to the beach.
2) Travel.
3) Socialize. Makes the experience way better.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: N/A

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Great friendship and memories. The life in America is truly amazing and different to living in Copenhagen.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Home sickness. Missing the closest people at home.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
